title: Nanoliposomal curcumin as a potential pro-apoptotic agent for cervical cancer: Evidence from Bcl-2 and Bax modulation in HeLa cells.
authors: Subandi, Subandi; Aisyah, Oktalia N; Lestari, Bayu
one_liner_zh: 该文研究纳米脂质体姜黄素对宫颈癌细胞凋亡蛋白Bcl-2/Bax的调控，与cpcdh基因家族无直接关联。
abstract: Cervical cancer remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality, and treatment effectiveness is often limited by drug resistance and systemic toxicity. Curcumin has shown anticancer activity, but its clinical translation is constrained by poor solubility and low bioavailability. Nanoliposomal curcumin (Cur-NLPs) may improve intracellular delivery; however, its dose-dependent effect on apoptosis-related proteins in cervical cancer cells remains insufficiently defined. This study evaluated the dose-dependent modulation of Bcl-2 and Bax protein expression by Cur-NLPs in HeLa cells. HeLa cells were assigned to five groups: negative control, cisplatin 5 microg/mL as positive control, and Cur-NLPs at 100, 150, and 200 microg/mL. After 24 hours of treatment, Bcl-2 and Bax expression were assessed by immunofluorescence and quantified as corrected total cell fluorescence (CTCF). Data were analyzed using one-way ANOVA, Tukey HSD post hoc test, Pearson correlation, and linear regression. Significant between-group differences were observed for both Bcl-2 (F=8.99; p=0.002) and Bax (F=132.38; p<0.001). Cur-NLPs progressively reduced Bcl-2 expression and increased Bax expression, with the most pronounced effect observed at 200 microg/mL. Bcl-2 expression at 200 microg/mL and Bax expression at 150-200 microg/mL were significantly altered compared with the negative control, while the 200 microg/mL dose showed no significant difference from cisplatin for either marker. Cur-NLPs concentration showed a strong negative correlation with Bcl-2 expression (r=-0.847; p<0.001) and a strong positive correlation with Bax expression (r=0.942; p<0.001). Linear regression further confirmed dose-dependent effects, with Cur-NLPs concentration explaining 79.6% and 88.8% of the variance in Bcl-2 and Bax expression, respectively. These findings indicate that Cur-NLPs can shift the Bcl-2/Bax balance toward a pro-apoptotic profile in HeLa cells, supporting its potential as a curcumin-based nanodelivery strategy for cervical cancer. Further studies using functional apoptosis assays, additional cervical cancer cell lines, and in vivo models are needed to confirm its translational relevance.
abstract_zh: 宫颈癌仍然是癌症相关死亡的主要原因之一，而治疗效果常受限于耐药性和全身毒性。姜黄素（curcumin）已显示出抗癌活性，但其临床转化受制于溶解性差和生物利用度低。纳米脂质体姜黄素（nanoliposomal curcumin, Cur-NLPs）可能改善细胞内递送；然而，其对宫颈癌细胞中凋亡相关蛋白的剂量依赖性效应仍未得到充分定义。本研究评估了Cur-NLPs在HeLa细胞中对Bcl-2和Bax蛋白表达的剂量依赖性调节作用。HeLa细胞被分为五组：阴性对照组、顺铂（cisplatin）5微克/毫升作为阳性对照组，以及Cur-NLPs 100、150和200微克/毫升组。处理24小时后，通过免疫荧光（immunofluorescence）评估Bcl-2和Bax表达，并量化为校正总细胞荧光（corrected total cell fluorescence, CTCF）。数据采用单因素方差分析（one-way ANOVA）、Tukey HSD事后检验、Pearson相关分析和线性回归进行分析。Bcl-2（F=8.99；p=0.002）和Bax（F=132.38；p<0.001）均观察到显著的组间差异。Cur-NLPs逐渐降低Bcl-2表达并增加Bax表达，在200微克/毫升时观察到最显著的效果。与阴性对照组相比，200微克/毫升时的Bcl-2表达和150-200微克/毫升时的Bax表达显著改变，而200微克/毫升剂量在两种标志物上与顺铂相比均无显著差异。Cur-NLPs浓度与Bcl-2表达呈强负相关（r=-0.847；p<0.001），与Bax表达呈强正相关（r=0.942；p<0.001）。线性回归进一步确认了剂量依赖性效应，Cur-NLPs浓度分别解释了Bcl-2和Bax表达变异的79.6%和88.8%。这些发现表明，Cur-NLPs能在HeLa细胞中将Bcl-2/Bax平衡转向促凋亡特征，支持其作为基于姜黄素的纳米递送策略用于宫颈癌的潜力。未来需采用功能性凋亡检测、更多宫颈癌细胞系和体内模型进行进一步研究，以确认其转化相关性。
